glm.feedback:
## Findings

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: medium
  File: client/e2e/flows/lead-inventory-page.spec.ts:105-111 (`withinLastNight`)
  Finding: The E2E re-implements the "last night" window with its own anchor math instead of reusing `computeLastNightWindow` (which `LeadInventoryPage.test.tsx` correctly uses via midpoint). When the suite runs between 00:00 and 06:00, `anchor` becomes *yesterday* 06:00, so the fixture timestamp is *yesterday 03:00*. If `computeLastNightWindow` at pre-dawn "now" returns the in-progress night `[yesterday 18:00, today 06:00]` (the natural reading of the spec's "18:00→06:00" window, and what the BeatList test comment documents for a 10:00 `now`), yesterday 03:00 is **outside** the window — `BeatList` filters the beat out and both E2E cases fail. The helper's own comment ("03:00 local on the calendar day whose 06:00 has not yet passed") contradicts its code, which in that branch yields a timestamp on the day whose 06:00 *has* passed — a sign the two were never reconciled. This is a time-of-day-dependent flake the ledger's single daytime "PASSED" run cannot have exercised.
  Suggestion: Compute the fixture timestamp as the midpoint of the actual `computeLastNightWindow(new Date())` (imported from `client/src/lib/auditTimelineMerge`), exactly as the page-level test does, and delete the hand-rolled anchor logic.

- Category: test
  Severity: medium
  File: server/src/external/org/charter-authority-read.test.ts:87-96 (`charterAuthorityCore` describe block)
  Finding: AC-4-agent requires the 2-of-4-declared case to be verified against a fixture charter via `GET /api/org/inventory`. The 2-of-4 case is only tested at the `extractBandSections` level; `charterAuthorityCore` itself is only tested with 4/4, a 404, and a custom path, and the route-level test also only exercises a 4/4 charter. A wiring bug in `charterAuthorityCore` (e.g., miscounting `declaredCount`, or dropping `bands` for a partially-declared charter) would pass the current suite.
  Suggestion: Add one `charterAuthorityCore` (or route-level) case with a 2-of-4 charter asserting `declaredCount === 2`, the two `declared:true` bands carrying prose, and the other two `declared:false`/`text:null`.

- Category: bug
  Severity: low
  File: server/src/routes/org-inventory-composite.ts:96-101
  Finding: The "found is monotone even if the scan itself later degraded to unknown" branch is dead code: `readBeatEffectAuditCore` always returns an **empty** `unclaimedBeatIds` whenever `status === "unknown"` (both non-200 return paths construct `new Set()`), so `auditResult.unclaimedBeatIds.has(entry.beatId)` can never be true on an unknown result. The runtime behavior is correct (unknown → unknown), but the comment (repeated in `beat-effect-audit-read.ts`'s header) documents a guarantee the code does not and cannot provide, and the type permits a state no producer creates.
  Suggestion: Either remove the comment/branch, or actually preserve partial findings in `readBeatEffectAuditCore`'s unknown path (which its own header also claims) — pick one; as written the two headers and the composite disagree with the implementation.

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: low
  File: client/src/components/leadInventory/BeatList.tsx:110 (`data-testid="unclaimed-effect-warning"`)
  Finding: The warning testid is not beat-scoped (unlike every other per-beat testid in the component: `beat-card-${beatId}`, `beat-steps-${beatId}`, `unclaimed-effect-unknown-${beatId}`). With two or more warned beats on one lead's list, `getByTestId` (Playwright strict mode, RTL `getBy`) fails on ambiguity — the E2E and component tests only pass because their fixtures have exactly one warned beat.
  Suggestion: Scope it (`unclaimed-effect-warning-${beat.beatId}`) or assert via `getAllByTestId` where multiple warnings are possible; keep the spec's literal `data-testid="unclaimed-effect-warning"` requirement satisfied by making the per-beat id a prefix or adding a stable wrapper.

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: low
  File: server/src/external/org/charter-authority-read.ts:106-124 (`extractSectionProse`)
  Finding: An unbalanced code fence in a band section (a single ``` line with no closer before the next heading) leaves `inCodeFence` true for the remainder of the section, silently swallowing all of that band's prose — the band renders as declared with `(no prose in this section)` even though prose exists. A hand-edited charter (the stated premise for this file's boundary probes) can easily contain this.
  Suggestion: Reset `inCodeFence` at section boundaries (it is per-call today but the toggle can straddle), or treat a fence-open at section start as prose-safe by bounding the scan to the already-sliced section lines and ignoring an unterminated fence state at the end.

## Verified-sound areas (checked, no defect)

- The two new readers (`beat-steps-read.ts`, `registerEntriesGuarded`) correctly validate `leadId`/`beatId` before path construction, use open-first `O_NOFOLLOW` + `fstat` + `realPathGuard`, and the refusal-before-fs-call tests genuinely prove it via the mocked `openSync` spy.
- The `auditLogCore` → `readAuditLinesGuarded` refactor preserves pagination semantics (same slicing, `nextCursor`, error statuses); the AC-9 single-scan rewrite genuinely removes the truncation axis.
- The tri-state degrade discipline (steps `ok`/`unreadable`, audit `clear`/`found`/`unknown`, register `ok`/`unreadable`) is never collapsed into a positive claim anywhere in the composite or UI, matching AC-2b/AC-9/AC-10.
- The `beat-register.ts` → `beat-register-health.ts` split updates all visible importers (`routes.ts`, `org-leads-composite.ts`, both test files) and preserves the route path and response shapes.
- The E2E data-safety guard is now unconditional (the `SHIPWRIGHT_LEADS_ROOT` bypass the doubt review flagged is closed) and checks the actual resolved target, not a `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` proxy.

## Overall assessment

Ship-with-fixes: the core implementation is solid and the degrade/security discipline is genuinely enforced, but the E2E's hand-rolled `withinLastNight` is a real time-of-day-dependent failure waiting to happen (and its comment contradicts its own code), and AC-4's 2-of-4 case is never exercised through `charterAuthorityCore` or the endpoint. Both are small, contained fixes.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
